leads.summary: Coordinate the output-row type with open PR #12658 before either PR merges
leads.consequence: #12658 projects output Repeater rows to {id,name} primitives to avoid dangling PwNode references, whereas this PR passes PwNode objects to groupedSinks and SinkRow. The independently merged Panel has two conflict blocks at refresh and output delegate. Resolving by retaining this PR's node rows discards #12658's safety change; resolving by using the primitive rows directly makes the row label a raw node.name and passes a non-PwNode to setDefaultSink unless the grouping, row lookup, row label and activation are all adapted. Both PRs' Node tests alone would miss the QML contract. #12658 is diverged (not stacked) and GitHub reports it MERGEABLE against its base, which is not a guarantee about the combined PRs.
leads.triage: already in Opus final; corroborated by Opus plan-11 merge (2 conflicts)

leads.summary: Coordinate the output-row type with open PR #12489's per-jack entries
leads.consequence: #12489 replaces displayAudioSinks with displayOutputEntries containing {node,port}, adds per-port active highlighting and setDefaultOutput. This PR groups bare PwNodes and replaces the same delegate. The independent merged Panel has three conflict blocks at refresh, delegate and label. Keeping this PR's side silently loses selection of individual ports; keeping #12489's entries without adapting sinkGroup, sinkRowLabel and the model collector loses grouping and AirPlay suffixes. Need group entry.node and preserve the port in activation and row label. #12489 is diverged and MERGEABLE against its base, not a clean combined merge.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator read coord/related/12489.diff (displayAudioSinks entry rows); Opus plan-11: 3 conflicts, entries classified OTHER/'Unknown'

leads.summary: Open PR #13212 will announce identical names for visually disambiguated AirPlay speakers
leads.consequence: #13212 adds Accessible.name: node ? root.nodeLabel(node) : ''. That cleanly merges with this PR's visible Text binding to Model.sinkRowLabel(...). Two devices advertised as Kitchen are visually 'Kitchen · WiiM Amp' and 'Kitchen · HomePod mini', but both screen-reader list items remain 'Kitchen', defeating the disambiguation for accessibility users. Use the same resolved row label for Accessible.name. #13212 is diverged, and GitHub reports MERGEABLE against its base; merged Panel.qml had zero conflict markers and differs from both inputs.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified coord/related/13212.diff SinkRow accessibleName: root.nodeLabel(node); Opus plan-11 clean merge

leads.summary: A discovered RAOP hostname outside .local leaves identical speakers with empty suffixes
leads.consequence: PipeWire passes the Avahi resolver's host_name verbatim to raop.hostname and, unless overridden, to node.name. The new script prints Kitchen.example.com and its model, but airPlayHostname() only matches a node name containing '.local.' and returns ''. With two same-description receivers whose target hostnames are Kitchen.example.com and Kitchen2.example.com, sinkRowLabel returns 'Kitchen · ' for both, including after the model collector succeeds. A hostname without .local or a manually loaded raop-sink with a non-local host has the same effect. Extract the hostname independently of the DNS suffix (or correlate module/node explicitly), and keep a nonempty unique fallback.
leads.triage: already an Opus minor note; rare

leads.summary: A supported RAOP node.name override makes an AirPlay speaker disappear from the AIRPLAY classification
leads.consequence: PipeWire raop-discover's create-stream rule merges user properties into the module arguments, and raop-sink sets its default raop_sink.* node.name only if no node.name was supplied. For a valid user rule giving the RAOP node a custom name, the node remains a playable sink, but this PR classifies it OTHER. If it is the only RAOP receiver the model script never launches; if another default-named RAOP receiver shares its display name, both rows remain unsuffixed because each is excluded from the other's AIRPLAY twin set. The node's .properties can be unsafe before binding; solve using a safe stable identifier or make the helper provide a node mapping for such custom names rather than assuming an unconditional factory prefix.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up-1 Q2 confirmed, judged uncommon and cosmetic

leads.summary: A failing pw-dump is reported as a successful empty discovery and erases good model labels
leads.consequence: Because the bash script has no pipefail, a pw-dump failure with no stdout produces an empty jq success and the helper exits 0. Quickshell's StdioCollector still emits streamFinished on process completion, and this panel assigns parseAirPlayModels('') => {}, discarding any previously valid models without signaling failure. Duplicate speakers are demoted to hostname-only labels until a later successful refresh. Propagate command errors and retain the last known map on a failed process; distinguish empty successful discovery from error.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up-1 Q1 confirmed (plan-9), transient

leads.summary: The new audio tests do not exercise the model collector or the QML presentation that implements the feature
leads.consequence: A plausible mutant changing the new script's jq filter to return no rows, or deleting the new QML Process and heading Text, still passes all new Model.js assertions: the test supplies the final tab-delimited string itself and does not read the new script or Panel.qml. Consequently the non-.local case and failing pw-dump case survive the test suite. Add a synthetic pw-dump module object/string stub in an isolated shell test, assert helper stdout/errors, and add a panel-level source/fixture or component assertion for the Process, heading and row binding. This is a test-fidelity issue, not evidence that the existing Model.js assertions fail.
leads.triage: already in Opus final F3; published only the demonstrated surviving mutant

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the AirPlay path works as described. PipeWire 1.6.9 source shows that raop-discover passes the receiver's `am` value to each raop-sink module as `device.model`, and that raop-sink names the node `raop_sink.<hostname>.<ip>.<port>` without copying `device.model` onto it. A real `pw-dump` against a private daemon printed module `args` as a JSON string, so the script's `fromjson` branch is the one that runs. In an offscreen load of the real `Panel.qml` with synthetic sinks, grouping, same-name labels (`Kitchen · WiiM Amp`, `Kitchen · HomePod mini`, `Pool` unchanged) and keyboard navigation behaved as described, headings were never cursor stops, and a single-group list laid out exactly as on `quattro`. The `friendlyAirPlayModel` mappings agree with pyatv's model identifier table, except `AudioAccessorySingle5,1`, which pyatv lists as HomePod mini and this PR labels "HomePod".

One stated behaviour does not hold: headings and regrouping also appear on machines without AirPlay.

### Headings appear without AirPlay when Omarchy's speaker tuning is present

`sinkGroup` puts every sink that is not `alsa_output.`, `bluez_output.` or `raop_sink.` into OTHER, and `showHeading` only checks that more than one group exists. Omarchy's own speaker tuning sink, `omarchy_speaker_tuning` ("Laptop Speakers"), therefore lands in OTHER. It is applied automatically at first run on the Dell XPS 14/16 (2026), and `omarchy-audio-sink-availability` hides the physical speaker sink it fronts, so it is the laptop's only speaker row.

Offscreen load of `Panel.qml`, synthetic sinks `[Headphones (alsa_output…), Laptop Speakers (omarchy_speaker_tuning)]`, no AirPlay (the same input order on both sides; on a real system the `quattro` order follows PipeWire registration):

```text
quattro                      this PR
-------                      -------
Headphones                   DIRECT
Laptop Speakers                Headphones
                             OTHER
                               Laptop Speakers
```

**Impact:** on those laptops, connecting headphones, a monitor with audio, Bluetooth or a USB DAC adds DIRECT/OTHER headings and moves the internal speakers to the bottom under OTHER, contradicting "a machine without AirPlay discovery looks exactly as it does today" and the `Model.js` comment saying so. With AirPlay present, "Laptop Speakers" sits below every AirPlay receiver. A virtual sink such as EasyEffects next to a sound card produces the same headings. Selection, volume and the default-sink highlight are unaffected.

**Suggested change** (either or both):
- Regroup and draw headings only when `Model.hasAirPlaySinks(...)` is true.
- Classify `omarchy_speaker_tuning` as DIRECT, since it stands in for the hidden internal speakers. The grouping test in `audio-test.sh` currently expects it last, so it would need updating.

### Smaller points

**Model lookup with `stream.props` rules:** if a raop-discover `stream.rules` action includes a `stream.props = { ... }` object (as in the module's documented example), that value is copied into the raop-sink args as raw SPA-JSON. `fromjson` then fails and those receivers silently fall back to hostname suffixes. Reproduced with the script's jq filter on synthetic dumps and on a real `pw-dump` of module args in raop-discover's format; the stock `50-raop.conf` and scalar-only rules (such as PR #9221's) are unaffected. Extracting the two keys without full JSON parsing (for example a jq `capture` on `"raop.hostname": "..."` and `"device.model": "..."`), or documenting the limit, would cover it.

**Optional:** the script exits 0 with empty output when `pw-dump` fails, and `onStreamFinished` then replaces `airPlayModels` with `{}`. In an offscreen panel run with a stub `pw-dump`, one failed or empty call turned `Kitchen · WiiM Amp` into `Kitchen · Kitchen` until the next successful refresh (the panel reruns it every 5 s). Keeping the previous map when the output is empty would avoid the flicker.

**Optional test improvement:** the new tests pass at head (34 ok) and fail at the merge-base for the right reason. However, a mutant where `sinkGroupCount` always returns 1 still passes, so heading visibility is untested. An assertion for a multi-group list, including the tuning-plus-headphones case above, would pin the intended behaviour.

**Overlapping open PRs:** #12489 and #12658 conflict with this PR in `Panel.qml`; #12231 and #13212 merge cleanly but interact with it.
- #12231 also reorders outputs (local before network) and keeps the speaker tuning with the local outputs.
- #12658 changes `displayAudioSinks` to `{ id, name }` rows. A merge that keeps both changes would sort AirPlay rows by hostname and lose every duplicate-name suffix, because `groupedSinks` and `sinkRowLabel` read `description` and object identity from that list.
- #12489 changes the sink rows to `{ node, port }` entries (one per plugged-in jack on multi-port sinks). Fed those entries, `groupedSinks` puts every row in OTHER and `sinkRowLabel` returns "Unknown".
- #13212 sets each sink row's `accessibleName` to `root.nodeLabel(node)`. Combined with this PR, two "Kitchen" speakers with different visible suffixes would both be announced as "Kitchen"; reusing `Model.sinkRowLabel(...)` there would keep them distinct.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of head `5f901e9` against PipeWire 1.6.9 and Quickshell source; `audio-test.sh` run in an isolated sandbox at head and merge-base, `bin-style-test.sh` and `qml-text-format-test.sh` at head, plus mutation runs; the script run against a stub `pw-dump`, and its jq filter against a real `pw-dump` from a private PipeWire daemon (no raop modules installed, so raop-format module args were loaded on a stand-in module); `Panel.qml` loaded offscreen with synthetic sinks and a stand-in for `KeyboardPanel`. No real AirPlay receivers, compositor or pixel rendering; `bar-widget-contract-test.sh` skipped without a compositor.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
